title: L0182
description: A compiled L0182 survey: what the survey asks, read from its own data by the compiler, and — once something has answered — the response to it. A survey has one of two styles: ranked-choice (options to choose, rank, and add one write-in to) or rating (items each answered on a scale).

survey.description: What the survey asks. None of it is written in the program: the compiler reads it from the survey the program names.

response.description: The answer to this survey. Absent until something answers. Written in code — by a person in the editor, or by an agent through update_item — so both clients produce the identical shape. Its shape follows the survey's style.

id.description: The survey being taken, as the program named it. Ties a response back to the survey it answers.

sessionId.description: One taking of the survey. Seeded from the item id, and what keeps a response with the version of the survey it answers. Absent when the program named no session.

instance.description: Which version of the survey was taken — the file it came from, e.g. civic-priorities-7. A survey with several versions draws one of them per session; writing this as the id takes that version outright.

instructions.description: What the participant is asked to do, shown under the title. Always present: the compiler substitutes a generic line when the survey's data supplies none.

style.description: Pick some options, rank them, and optionally add a write-in.

options.description: The set a response is chosen from, compiled in from the survey's own data. A program cannot write it.

minChoices.description: Fewest options a response may choose. The survey's own, defaulting to 1. Enforced by the compiler, which is the only enforcement there is — nothing renders a survey interactively.

maxChoices.description: Most options a response may choose. The survey's own; never more than the number of options, defaulting to 5, or one fewer than the set when the set is smaller, so a default never permits choosing every option.

option.title: Option
option.description: One option in the set. The id is the originating service's own where the survey's data carried one, and positional (o0 upward) where it did not — a response names ids, never text.

choices.description: The ids of the options chosen, in priority order. The order IS the ranking, first is most important. Empty when only a write-in was contributed. Source may name an option by its text, its id, or its position; the compiler resolves all three, so compiled output is always ids.

writeIn.description: One new option from whoever answered, which was not already in the set.

style.description: Answer each item on its scale — Likert, NPS, stars, semantic differential — and optionally add a comment.

items.description: The statements or questions to rate, in order, compiled in from the survey's own data. A program cannot write them.

comment.description: Present when the survey asks for a free-text comment.

item.title: Item
item.description: One statement or question, with its scale resolved inline. The id is the survey's own where its data carried one, and positional (q0 upward) where it did not.

required.description: Whether a response must answer it. An opt-out counts as an answer.

anchors.description: This item's own words for the low and high ends of its scale — a semantic differential.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: Every scale form — a preset, labelled points, a numeric range — compiled to one list of points.

name.description: The preset or named scale this came from. Items sharing one form a grid.

label.description: The words for this point, where it has any.

optOut.description: An answer outside the scale, such as Not applicable. Recorded as an opt-out, never a value.

ratings.description: One answer per item answered, in the survey's item order. Source may name an item by its text, id or position and answer by a point's label or the scale's value; compiled output is always ids and values.

comment.description: Free text, where the survey asks for a comment.
